core_assessment: I read statement192-194 and the complete proof376-475, including the native TikZ coordinates, before selector difficulty fields. The operative inequalities are all C points left of all A points left of all B points, all A below all B/C, B indexed in increasing height and decreasing x, and the entire C_j group above b_j and below b_(j+1), with C_m above all B. The C points follow a single increasing-x/increasing-y diagonal, so the C groups are ordered in x as well as height. Finite copies can be horizontally scaled into disjoint strips around the base anchors; all non-anchor points are above the common base line. A rectangle with top between the base line and every other point captures exactly the m base points P. Within any strip, B_i is isolated by the x-gap from A_i and C_i; each C_i,j is isolated by its own x-interval. These are exact m-point edges. A hit in P fixes i. In Case1 choose a hit b_j in B_i and a hit c_j^l in C_i,j. Place the left boundary immediately before c_j^l in the global increasing C order, the top immediately above it in the same order, and the right boundary immediately to the right of b_j but left of the preceding B point when j>1. Earlier C points are excluded by the left boundary and later C points by the top. Lower-index B points are farther right and excluded by the right boundary; higher-index B points are above C_j and excluded by the top. All A points remain between the horizontal bounds and below the top. Thus this exact trace is A_i union {b_j,c_j^l}, of size (m-2)+1+1=m, and it contains at least4 hits. The same boundary reasoning handles j=1 and j=m. In Case2 put the left boundary between the leftmost anchor and the next A point, thereby excluding the anchor and every C point. For any consecutive B indices t,t+1,t+2, put the right boundary just right of b_t and the top just above b_(t+2); the opposite B coordinate orders isolate exactly that triple. The rectangle captures precisely the m-3 non-anchor A points plus those3 B points. Since its A points have no hits, every consecutive B-triple must be hit. The four disjoint triples among indices1 through12 require4 distinct hits in B_i, contradicting shallowness of the exact m-edge B_i. This covers all m>=12, including m=12 and triples at either endpoint. Every local boundary can remain inside its gadget strip, so no other gadget or anchor enters these traces. Contradicting shallowness on this explicitly verified set of edges suffices for the full family of all exact m-point traces; other traces cannot restore a shallow hitting set.
